topic.angle: Water bears survived exposure to vacuum in a 2007 orbital experiment

body.question: In 2007, tardigrades were taken into orbit and exposed to the vacuum of space. For how long?
body.reveal: For 10 days, on the 2007 FOTON-M3 mission. Back on Earth, the dehydrated tardigrades were revived just by adding water. The space vacuum did not much affect their egg-laying.

probes.question: True or false: tardigrades exposed to space vacuum in 2007 were revived by rehydration back on Earth.
The 2007 tardigrade experiment flew on the ____ mission.

image_brief.show: A microscope image of a tardigrade (water bear)

claims.claim: In 2007 tardigrades were taken into orbit on FOTON-M3 and exposed to the vacuum of space for 10 days (question, answer 10 days, reveal)
claims.quote: began in 2007 with the FOTON-M3 mission in low Earth orbit , where they were exposed to space's vacuum for 10 days

claims.claim: Back on Earth the tardigrades were revived just by rehydration (reveal, probe p1 true)
claims.quote: and reanimated, just by rehydration, back on Earth

claims.claim: Probe p2: the 2007 tardigrade experiment flew on the FOTON-M3 mission
claims.quote: The 2007 FOTON-M3 mission carrying the BIOPAN astrobiology payload (illustrated) exposed tardigrades to vacuum

claims.claim: The space vacuum did not much affect their egg-laying (reveal last sentence)
claims.quote: The space vacuum did not much affect egg-laying in either Richtersius coronifer or M. tardigradum
claims.note: Page also says vacuum plus full solar UV sharply reduced survival; the card sentence is only about egg-laying, which matches.
